dublinCore.title: Probability Distribution Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Probability theory
Random variables
Statistical distributions
Mean and expected value
Variance
Standard deviation
Central limit theorem
dublinCore.description: Interactive MicroSim that draws N seeded random samples from a uniform, Gaussian, exponential, binomial (Bernoulli) or Poisson distribution, or from the sum of n uniform variables, and overlays their histogram on the theoretical PDF/PMF (or the empirical CDF on the CDF). A band marks mu +/- k sigma with its probability, and a table compares the theoretical and sample mean, variance and standard deviation. The central-limit mode shows the sum of n uniforms approaching a Gaussian.

learningObjectives: Explain the difference between a PDF or PMF and a CDF, and compute an interval probability as F(b) - F(a)
Calculate the mean, variance and standard deviation of the uniform, Gaussian, exponential, binomial and Poisson distributions from their parameters
Apply the 68-95-99.7 rule to Gaussian signals and compare it with the band probabilities of non-Gaussian distributions
Describe how the sample mean and variance approach the true values as N grows, using the standard error sigma/sqrt(N)
Explain the central limit theorem by observing that a sum of n uniform variables approaches a Gaussian with mean n/2 and variance n/12
prerequisites: Definitions of mean, variance and standard deviation

misconceptions.misconception: 68% of the values always lie within one standard deviation of the mean
misconceptions.correction: The 68-95-99.7 rule is a property of the Gaussian; other distributions put different probabilities in mu +/- k sigma
misconceptions.evidence: At k = 1 the band holds 0.683 for the Gaussian but 0.577 for the uniform, 0.865 for the exponential and 0.798 for Poisson with lambda = 4; the sum of n uniforms approaches 0.683 as n grows

misconceptions.misconception: The sample mean and variance are the mean and variance of the distribution
misconceptions.correction: Sample statistics are estimates that fluctuate from sample to sample; the error of the sample mean shrinks like sigma/sqrt(N)
misconceptions.evidence: With N = 10 samples of N(0, 1) the sample mean is -0.285 and the sample variance 1.473; at N = 10000 they are 0.016 and 0.998

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Probability distribution explorer. A plot shows the theoretical PDF or PMF in maroon with a blue histogram of N random samples, or the theoretical and empirical CDFs, and a gold band marks the mean plus or minus k standard deviations with the probability it contains. A table compares the theoretical and sample mean, variance and standard deviation. Controls choose the distribution, its parameters, the number of samples, the band width k, a CDF view, a Gaussian overlay and new samples.

controls.label: Distribution
controls.description: Chooses the distribution that is sampled

controls.label: First parameter (a, mu, lambda, n or terms n)
controls.description: Uniform lower limit a (-5 to 5), Gaussian mean mu (-3 to 3), exponential rate lambda (0.25 to 4), binomial trials n (1 to 50), Poisson mean lambda (0.5 to 20) or the number of uniform terms n (1 to 30); the range changes with the distribution

controls.label: Second parameter (b, sigma or p)
controls.description: Uniform upper limit b (-5 to 5, kept at least 0.2 above a), Gaussian standard deviation sigma (0.25 to 2.5) or binomial success probability p (0.01 to 0.99); hidden for one-parameter distributions

controls.label: Samples N
controls.description: Number of samples used, stepping through 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000 and 10000; a larger N keeps the earlier samples

controls.label: Band k
controls.description: Half-width of the shaded band mu +/- k sigma, in standard deviations

controls.label: Show CDF
controls.description: Switches from the PDF/PMF and histogram to the theoretical CDF and the empirical CDF

controls.label: Gaussian overlay
controls.description: Adds the Gaussian density (or CDF) with the same mean and variance as a dashed green curve

controls.label: New samples
controls.description: Draws a new set of samples by advancing the random seed by one

visualElements.description: Theoretical PDF or PMF (maroon) with the histogram or relative frequencies of the samples (blue), the mu +/- k sigma band with its probability (gold), the mean line and an optional Gaussian overlay (green); or the theoretical and empirical CDFs with the band edges and Delta F

Table of theoretical and sample mean, variance, standard deviation and band probability, with the standard error of the mean, the band limits and, in CLT mode, the largest gap between the exact CDF and the Gaussian CDF

model.description: Each distribution draws one seeded stream of 10000 samples and the first N are used. Theoretical moments and band probabilities come from closed-form PDFs, PMFs and CDFs; the CLT mode uses the exact Irwin-Hall distribution of a sum of n U(0, 1) variables.
equations: Gaussian: f(x) = exp(-(x - mu)^2/(2 sigma^2)) / (sigma sqrt(2 pi)), P(|X - mu| <= k sigma) = erf(k/sqrt 2)
Exponential: f(x) = lambda exp(-lambda x), E[X] = 1/lambda, Var(X) = 1/lambda^2
Binomial: P(X = j) = C(n, j) p^j (1 - p)^(n - j), E[X] = np, Var(X) = np(1 - p)
Poisson: P(X = j) = lambda^j e^(-lambda) / j!, E[X] = Var(X) = lambda
Sum of n uniforms: E[S] = n/2, Var(S) = n/12
P(mu - k sigma <= X <= mu + k sigma) = F(mu + k sigma) - F(mu - k sigma)
Sample variance s^2 = sum (x_i - xbar)^2 / (N - 1); standard error of the mean = sigma / sqrt(N)
algorithms: Mulberry32 seeded uniform generator with a MurmurHash3-finalized seed per distribution
Sum of n Bernoulli trials for the binomial; Knuth's multiplication method for the Poisson
Cox-de Boor recursion for the cardinal B-spline (Irwin-Hall) PDF and CDF
Histogram bin width by Scott's rule h = 3.49 sigma N^(-1/3)
limitations: Axes are fixed per distribution, so very wide settings (for example an exponential with lambda = 0.25) put some samples beyond the plot; the panel reports how many
Band probabilities use the closed interval, which matters for the discrete distributions

instructionalStrategies: Predict the band probability before reading it
Compare distributions with the same mean and variance
Increase N to watch sample statistics converge
Step n in CLT mode and record the Gaussian gap
extensions: Add a Rayleigh distribution for fading envelopes
Add sums of exponential or Bernoulli variables to the CLT mode
Plot the sample mean against N on a log axis
